workloads.label: Bursty API or event handlers
workloads.detail: Demand changes quickly and each invocation is short-lived and stateless.

workloads.label: Steady long-running service
workloads.detail: Traffic is predictable and the process needs stable runtime behavior.

workloads.label: Custom or legacy runtime
workloads.detail: The application needs host-level agents, unusual networking, or an unsupported runtime.

constraints.label: Minimize routine operations
constraints.detail: Prefer a smaller patching, scaling, and control-plane burden.

constraints.label: Keep the runtime portable
constraints.detail: Reduce dependence on a provider-specific execution contract.

constraints.label: Control the platform boundary
constraints.detail: Host agents, network policy, scheduling, or runtime tuning are first-class needs.

teams.label: Small generalist team
teams.detail: The same engineers build features and operate production.

teams.label: Experienced platform team
teams.detail: The team already operates clusters, policy, upgrades, and shared observability.

teams.label: Migration-focused operations team
teams.detail: Preserving an existing runtime is more important than immediate modernization.

providerPostures.label: Greenfield and provider-neutral
providerPostures.detail: No existing contract or geography decides the shortlist.
providerPostures.gate: Benchmark the same service role, workload, and recovery test in every eligible region.

providerPostures.label: Existing governed provider
providerPostures.detail: Identity, networking, support, and audit controls already exist in one cloud.
providerPostures.gate: Count existing controls as operating value, but require the incumbent to pass the same workload and recovery gates.

providerPostures.label: Required geography or residency
providerPostures.detail: Data and processing must remain in an approved location.
providerPostures.gate: Verify the exact service, dependencies, backups, support boundary, and recovery region in the approved geography.

serviceModels.label: Managed functions
serviceModels.examples: Lambda, Azure Functions, or Google Cloud functions
serviceModels.failure: Concurrency limits, startup delay, invocation timeouts, and event retries remain application concerns.
serviceModels.verify: Measure burst throttling, startup latency, maximum duration, retry duplication, and downstream connection pressure.

serviceModels.label: Managed container runtime
serviceModels.examples: ECS on Fargate or App Runner, Azure Container Apps, or Cloud Run
serviceModels.failure: Autoscaling, startup, health checks, and request termination still need explicit application behavior.
serviceModels.verify: Measure startup, concurrency, scale limits, private networking, deployment rollback, and connection draining.

serviceModels.label: Managed Kubernetes
serviceModels.failure: A managed control plane does not operate workloads, policies, nodes, upgrades, or application recovery for the team.
serviceModels.verify: Test upgrades, node loss, autoscaling, policy enforcement, stateful recovery, and platform-team on-call ownership.

serviceModels.label: Virtual machines
serviceModels.examples: EC2, Azure Virtual Machines, or Compute Engine
serviceModels.failure: The team owns operating-system lifecycle, process recovery, image hygiene, scaling, and host-level observability.
serviceModels.verify: Test image builds, patch rollout, replacement, autoscaling, backup restoration, and loss of a host or zone.
